svg.text: Orvanna purchase path, end to end
Twelve hops from an empty cart to a recorded sale. Every hop names the real file and the real function. Sandbox test mode only.
Blue = the visitor's browser. Purple = our server code. Brown = a third party. Read top to bottom.
The shopper fills a cart
www/shop.html, reading names, prices and volume points from www/js/catalog.js (the PRODUCTS array).
Nothing has left the browser yet. The cart lives in the browser's own local storage.
BROWSER
The page asks what it will really cost, before any card
POST quote-tax. File: functions/quote-tax/index.ts. It creates no order and no payment.
It reprices with priceCart() in _shared/pricing.ts, then calls calculateTax() in _shared/tax.ts.
OUR SERVER
Stripe Tax answers
The destination address comes from the member's row in our database, read by resolveTaxAddress().
If Stripe cannot be reached the cart still prices, at a flat five percent, marked as a fallback.
THIRD PARTY
The account step finishes, so the payment step opens itself
liveEnsureCheckout() in www/shop.html sends POST create-payment.
The request carries only sku, mode and quantity. No price, no total, no name, no address, no card.
BROWSER
create-payment runs the rails, reprices, and books the order
functions/create-payment/index.ts: checkRateLimit(), the daily ceiling, priceCart(), calculateTax(),
generateOrderNumber() making ORV-YYYY-MM-XXXXXX, then INSERT app.demo_orders with status created.
OUR SERVER
The same function opens the payment at HyperSwitch
POST /payments with the secret key, the amount in whole cents, and a return address built by
buildReturnUrl() on the server. The returned payment_id is stored on the row as payment_reference.
OUR SERVER
The browser mounts HyperSwitch's own card widget
loadHyperLoader() then window.Hyper(publishable key) in www/shop.html. The page shows the
server's totals, not its own. Card numbers are typed into HyperSwitch's frame, never into our page.
BROWSER
HyperSwitch routes the card to Braintree, and 3-D Secure runs
Usually silent. When the bank wants proof it draws a passcode window inside its own frame.
Our part is only the surrounding chrome: openChallengeChrome() in www/shop.html.
THIRD PARTY
The browser asks us what happened
POST confirm-payment carrying only { order_number }.
There is no status field in the request, so there is nothing for a hostile page to forge.
BROWSER
Our server asks the processor itself, and writes the truth
retrieveAndApplyPaymentTruth() in functions/_shared/edge.ts: GET /payments/{id} with the secret
key, mapHyperswitchStatus(), amount compared to the cent, then a guarded UPDATE.
OUR SERVER
The shopper sees the receipt the server wrote
The confirmation view renders from the response, not from the page's own arithmetic.
The cart is cleared on succeeded and on nothing else, so a decline keeps the cart for a retry.
BROWSER
The sale is booked with the tax engine, afterwards
POST record-tax, fired and forgotten by the page: functions/record-tax/index.ts turns the Stripe
calculation into a recorded transaction. Deliberately outside the payment path, and retryable.
OUR SERVER
The second door: payment-webhook
A shopper can approve a passcode and then
close the tab, so step 9 never happens.
HyperSwitch also calls us directly.
functions/payment-webhook/index.ts checks a
keyed signature first, and a bad one is refused
before a single database query runs.
A good one is still only a wake-up call: the
same step 10 function decides what is true.
What never travels to our server
No card number or security code.
No shopper name or street address.
No price and no total.
No raw network address; only a salted hash.
The billing address sent to the card networks
is one fixed invented address, not a person's.
The staff console takes the same path
www/staff.html is a phone-order version of the
same twelve hops, sending channel
staff_console instead of shop.
It carries its own copy of the payment code,
which is a known problem. See the gaps list.
Verified against the files on 2026-08-15.
MLM-PILOT/functions/ and MLM-PILOT/www/.
